profile.campus: LightEdge Des Moines campus, Altoona, IA (DC1 and DC2, adjacent buildings on Northridge Circle)
profile.reading: LightEdge Des Moines 2, also referred to as DC2, sits at 1401 Northridge Circle in Altoona, Iowa, immediately adjacent to the operator first Des Moines-area building on the same street. Per LightEdge own combined specification sheet for the two-building site, the pair together provide 6.1 megawatts of critical IT load and 10.6 megawatts of total generator capacity with N plus 1 UPS redundancy, across 78,000 total square feet including 40,000 square feet of white space, though the sheet does not break those totals down between DC1 and DC2 individually, so no single-building capacity or square footage figure is assigned to this record. A 2024 LightEdge leadership-transition announcement credits the company with building the first greenfield colocation data center in Iowa, though it does not name or date a specific building among the Des Moines site facilities, so that claim is presented as company-level context rather than attributed to DC2 specifically. The facility carries a broad compliance-oriented certification set common across LightEdge portfolio, including SOC 1, 2, and 3, ISO 27001, 20000-1, and 22301, HITRUST, HIPAA and HITECH readiness, PCI DSS, and NIST 800-53 and 800-171 alignment, with ten on-net carriers including Verizon, Lumen, Windstream, and Zayo. LightEdge Solutions was founded in 1996 and is headquartered in Des Moines, Iowa. LightEdge announced a new partnership with GI Partners, a private equity and real estate investment firm, in September 2021. LightEdge describes its current footprint as 20 data centers across 12 US metro markets plus a location in Amsterdam, Netherlands. No tenant is named for this specific building. Altoona sits just east of downtown Des Moines and has grown as a suburban technology and light-industrial corridor, a pattern consistent with LightEdge decision to concentrate its Iowa infrastructure there rather than in the city core, reflecting the same land and power availability considerations that shape data center site selection nationally.

reading.body:
LightEdge Des Moines 2 is one of two adjacent buildings on Northridge Circle in Altoona, Iowa, a suburban corridor east of Des Moines. The operator publishes combined specifications for both buildings but not individually, so this record accounts for a proportional share of the stated 6.1 megawatts of critical IT load and 10.6 megawatts of generator capacity across both sites. Assuming 40 kilowatts per rack as a typical colocation density, the combined 6.1 megawatts translates to approximately 150 racks; at higher AI training densities of 80 to 100 kilowatts per rack, the same power would support roughly 60 to 75 racks. The facility holds SOC 1, 2, and 3, ISO 27001, HITRUST, HIPAA readiness, PCI DSS, and NIST alignment certifications. Ten on-net carriers including Verizon and Lumen serve the site.

Iowa has published capacity from only two data center operators, totaling 18 megawatts of IT load across 52 mapped facilities statewide. This campus ranks third in the state by announced megawatts, though the published figure combines two buildings and cannot be assigned to Des Moines 2 alone. The operator, LightEdge Solutions, operates 20 data centers across 12 US metro markets and describes itself as having built the first greenfield colocation data center in Iowa, though the specific building and date are not named in available announcements.

For AI scaling purposes, this campus matters only at colocation density and only if tenants choose to place workloads here. The power supply is fixed and modest in absolute terms. No tenant is named for Des Moines 2. No information is published about interconnect latency to major compute hubs, power cost, PUE efficiency, or whether the facility has been built out or remains available for lease. The grid constraint that binds AI scaling at the state level cannot be read from a single facility's published specs.
